The record's formation reads 'Verbo (forma simples) + でしょう' / 'Verb (plain form) + でしょう', and plain form includes the past, so a to-ta-form verb variant is added alongside the existing to-dictionary one. Noun and na-adjective append the token bare, which respects the record's explicit ban on a copula before でしょう (×高いですでしょう, and by the same logic no だ). points.resolution_note: The rejected rule is genuinely unsafe and cannot be narrowed inside the closed enums, so no steps are emitted. The defect both checkers raised is real: base:"noun" + append があります, executed on the mandated noun 学生, emits 学生があります, the precise error this record exists to prevent (its own nuance calls it 'o erro clássico de quem fala português'). The restriction that would fix it is animacy; the base enum's only nominal value is the unrestricted `noun`, inventing an inanimate-noun base is forbidden, and no combination of the closed ops filters a base by semantic class. A `partial` is not available either, because there is exactly one candidate base and it is the unsafe one. Emitting nothing is the right outcome here: the animacy restriction stays in the record's explanation, formation and nuance, where a human reader gets it, instead of being silently dropped from a machine rule that a drill generator would execute blind. nuance_tags left empty: the closed tag enum has no value for existence or animacy, and none of the available tags describes this point.
points.steps_unavailable: Animacy restriction not expressible. The record's formation is 'Substantivo (coisa) + が + あります' / 'Noun (thing) + が + あります', and the animate/inanimate split is the entire content of the point ('Use あります para coisas que não se movem por vontade própria; para pessoas e animais, usa-se います'). The base enum's only nominal value is the unrestricted `noun`, so every rule the enum can express also accepts 学生, 犬, 田中さん and emits 学生があります / 犬があります, which must be 学生がいます / 犬がいます. No inanimate-noun base exists and none may be invented, and no closed op filters a base by semantic class, so no step list is emitted. Same reason as gram:gp-12 (its plain-form counterpart), and mirrored in gram:ga-imasu / gram:gp-13.

points.resolution_note: Mirror of gram:ga-arimasu, resolved the same way. The rejected rule base:"noun" + append がいます happens to pass the mandated noun (学生がいます is correct), which is why one checker graded it major rather than critical, but it accepts the whole inanimate class and emits 本がいます / 机がいます / 車がいます, all of which require あります. The record delimits the base as explicitly as its counterpart does ('Substantivo (ser vivo)' / 'Noun (living thing)', 'Para o oposto (objetos, coisas sem vida) usa-se あります/ある'), and that restriction is animacy, which the base enum cannot carry. The second checker's structural point is what settles it, and it is the reason a rule that looks fine on the mandated test noun still cannot ship: ga-imasu and ga-arimasu were given byte-identical step shapes differing only in the appended token, so to a consumer reading formation_steps alone the two points are indistinguishable, the single contrast the pair exists to teach disappears, and a generator can freely produce both halves of the error pair. Emitting nothing keeps the contrast where it is actually stated, in the record's prose. nuance_tags left empty: no value in the closed enum covers existence or animacy.

points.resolution_note: Plain-form counterpart of gram:ga-arimasu, resolved identically and for the same reason. Both checkers agree and both are right: base:"noun" + append がある executed on the mandated noun 学生 emits 学生がある, the record's own headline mistake (correct: 学生がいる), and the record states the rule it violates in so many words ('o japonês escolhe o verbo de existência pela natureza do sujeito'). One checker pre-empts the obvious objection that every pattern carries semantics, and the distinction holds: gp-142 になる also takes base=noun but genuinely accepts any noun (本になる is fine), whereas here the record itself excludes a class. The exclusion is animacy, the base enum has only the unrestricted `noun`, and inventing a base value is forbidden, so nothing is emitted. A second, independent reason is worth recording: the record flags ある's suppletive negative ない ('não existe ×あらない'), a lexical irregularity that no ordered sequence of closed ops derives, so even the negative half of this record's formation would be out of reach. nuance_tags left empty: the closed enum carries no existence or animacy value.
